summary:
Tabs feature implemented but not executed: I did not run tests or repository code, so everything is verified only by reading.

Changes:
- src/textual/widgets/tabs.py (new): Tab, TabsRenderable, Tabs; __all__ = ["Tab", "Tabs"]. Not re-exported from textual.widgets.
- renderables/underline_bar.py: builds one Text object; clickable_ranges input placed before width; click spans appended last; zero-width early path adds none.
- renderables/opacity.py: blended color merged into existing style (style + blended), preserving meta.
- _layout_resolve.py: concrete EdgeSpec dataclass (size, min_size, fraction); layout_resolve unchanged.
- tests/renderables/test_underline_bar.py: two new tests appended; existing tests untouched.
- tests/widgets/test_tabs.py (new, with __init__.py): construction, names, duplicates, first-index lookup, label-row layout, auto-fit shares, click and dimming styles, activate methods.
- docs/reference/tabs.md, sandbox/tabs_demo.py and tabs_demo.css, CHANGELOG Unreleased entry.

Choices to review:
- Bar position uses the displayed-tab index rather than find_tab_by_name. These differ only with duplicate names; acceptance criterion 11 requires the underline under the displayed tab.
- Empty labels omit their label edge, because the resolver treats size 0 as flexible.
- can_focus = True on Tabs; without it the widget never receives key events. Not in the spec's attribute list.
- Escape calls app.set_focus(None) unawaited, as specified; it emits a never-awaited warning and does not remove focus.
- Tests read _active_tab_name and _bar_position directly, since there is no public getter.

Unverified risks:
- Click metadata surviving the Opacity merge depends on rich's Style addition keeping the left operand's meta. Rich source was not available to confirm; the inactive-tab click test will catch a failure.
- Pytest was not run, so new and existing underline tests are unconfirmed.
